tools.name: url_probe
tools.description: Check if a URL is up. Sends a HEAD request (GET fallback that reads at most 8 KB) to a public http(s) URL and returns the HTTP status code, ok true/false, final URL after redirects, content type, content length and response time in ms. A cheap uptime, health or broken-link check before a heavier fet

tools.name: page_extract
tools.description: Extract the readable text of a web page as clean markdown. Fetches one public http(s) HTML page and returns its main content as markdown, plus title, meta description, byline and a short excerpt, with menus and page clutter removed. Useful for summarizing, quoting, or feeding a page to an LLM or RAG

tools.name: watch_once
tools.description: Detect whether a web page has changed since the last check. Fetches a public URL, normalizes its main text and returns a sha256 hash, changed true/false against the previous_hash sent in (null on the first check), word count and fetch time. A one-shot change monitor for price, policy or docs pages.

tools.name: json_shape
tools.description: Turn messy text into structured JSON. Parses a JSON blob or key: value lines (up to 50,000 characters) into an object using the field names given in schema_hint, and returns notes on what matched. Rule-based parsing with no LLM, so results are fast and predictable. Useful for normalizing tool output

tools.name: brief
tools.description: Research brief with cited sources on any topic, written to order (not instant). Returns a job id and due time right away; the finished brief (title, summary, markdown body, source links, word count) is ready within 24 hours, usually the same day, at GET /v1/jobs/:id, which is free. tools.description: In-depth research report with cited sources, for decisions that need more than a quick note. About 1,500 words (1,200-2,000) with an executive summary, key findings and analysis, at least 8 cited public sources, and an operator check before delivery. tools.name: brief_status
tools.description: Free. Check a brief ordered with the brief or deep_brief tool. Delivered within 24h (usually same day): ~500 words by default (50–1500), at least 3 cited source links. Returns status, dueBy, and result {title, summary, body_markdown, sources, word_count} when done.

tools.name: tip_remaining
tools.description: When you're done with a pack, tip everything left on it (unused credits at the price paid + pack balance) to AUTOGROK Desk. No new charge; it clears the pack to zero and can't be undone. Needs header X-Entitlement-Key. Call with confirm=false (or omit) to see the amount; then confirm=true with expec

tools.name: support_request
tools.description: Open a support ticket with the people behind AUTOGROK Desk (payment or receipt, a failed job, credits, anything else). Send X-Entitlement-Key on the connection or include an email. Returns a ticket id like HELP-XXXX. No automatic reply is sent; a person answers, usually within 1 business day.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: url_probe, watch_once, support_request · Private data: url_probe, page_extract · Public sink: support_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: url_probe, watch_once, support_request · Private data: url_probe, page_extract · Public sink: support_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
